newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin doctor sees president working full term.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin doctor sees president working full term.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin should be able to work out his full term in office, provided his planned heart operation goes as well as doctors expect, the Kremlin's chief doctor was quoted as saying on Tuesday.

Sergei Mironov, head of the Kremlin's medical centre, told the daily Komsomolskaya Pravda that Yeltsin's medical team was ready for any problems which might arise during or after the operation, which will improve blood supply to Yeltsin's heart.

"If everything goes well, I mean the operation itself and the period after it, I am confident that Boris Nikolayevich (Yeltsin) will be able to work fully throughout his presidential term, and longer," Mironov said.
"Believe me, he is a strong and a powerful person."
Yeltsin, breaking a long Kremlin tradition of secrecy about the health of its leaders, said on September 5 he needed a heart bypass operation.
The announcement triggered a struggle for power within the Kremlin and the president last week appealed to his aides and ministers to work together.

Presidential press spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky said on Monday preparations for the operation had reached their final stage and that doctors had cancelled all Yeltsin's planned meetings while they carried out a final round of tests.
Yastrzhembsky said surgery would not take place this week.
Mironov, who has given a series of upbeat forecasts about the operation in the last weeks, said Yeltsin, 65, had never had kidney problems and any problems with his liver were "due to age".
"There were never any kidney problems, it is absolute disinformation," he said.
He said preparations for the operation were going according to schedule. "I think we are on the right track, we have made some progress," he said.
